title: NCAA and NAIA Eligibility for International Athletes: Step by Step
h1: NCAA and NAIA eligibility for international athletes: step by step
desc: Which eligibility center to register with (NCAA, NAIA, NJCAA), what each account costs for international students, the amateurism rules and the 5-year clock.
lead: A coach wanting you is not enough: an official body has to confirm that you meet the academic and amateurism requirements. This guide explains what to do and when, with a focus on athletes from outside the United States.
body:
Which center do I register with?

If you want to play in…You register with…
NCAA Division I or IIThe NCAA Eligibility Center (eligibilitycenter.org), academic and athletic certification account
NCAA Division IIIInternational students still need to certify amateurism through the athletic-only account
NAIAThe NAIA Eligibility Center (playnaia.org). It is separate: being registered with the NCAA is not enough
Junior college (NJCAA)There is no eligibility center, but you must have finished high school

NCAA account types and what they cost

Profile Page (free). Start here. It gives you an NCAA ID, which is worth putting in every email to a coach.

Academic and athletic certification account (USD 170 for international students). You need it for Division I or II, and it must be complete before official visits or signing. Most athletes pay for it when a coach shows real interest.

Athletic-only account (USD 75). For international athletes planning to play in Division III. Fee waivers depend on U.S. benefit programs, so in practice a student at a school outside the U.S. does not qualify.

NAIA in four steps

1. Create your profile at playnaia.org. 2. Your school sends your academic records to the NAIA Eligibility Center. 3. As an international student you buy the InCred evaluation (incredevals.org): only what InCred verifies counts. 4. When an NAIA coach adds you to their recruiting list, your case is evaluated with priority. International registration costs USD 170. To be eligible you need a 2.3 GPA or higher, or two of three: ACT 18 / SAT 970, a 2.0 GPA, or the top half of your class.

Timeline if your school year ends in December

In Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Paraguay high school ends in December, and U.S. classes start in August (or January for the second semester). Two years before graduating: create your Profile Page (and an NAIA profile if you are interested). A year and a half before: request your transcript from your school and find out how to get an official English translation. When a Division I or II coach gets serious: move to the paid account and upload your documents. At graduation: send the final certificate and proof of graduation; without them the evaluation cannot close.

The 5-year rule (Division I)

Since 2026, Division I gives you five seasons within five years. The clock starts with your first full-time enrollment at a college or the academic year in which you turn 19, whichever comes first, and it does not stop if you do not play or transfer. A long gap year after high school can cost you seasons, so plan to enroll the August after you graduate. Division II keeps the rule of four seasons in ten semesters.

Amateurism: where international athletes get tangled

In many countries youth teams and the first team share one club. The NCAA asks about signed contracts, payment beyond expenses or equipment, training or playing with a professional squad, and agents. Always answer truthfully: a false answer is far worse than a situation that can be explained. If in doubt, ask the NCAA before you register.

Rules change often, so confirm the current version on the official NCAA and NAIA websites.
faq: Do international students have to register with the NCAA Eligibility Center?
Yes, if they want to play in NCAA Division I or II, and also to certify amateurism for Division III. The NAIA has its own center, and junior colleges (NJCAA) have none.
How much does it cost to register as an international athlete?

The NCAA Profile Page is free. The academic and athletic certification account costs USD 170 for international students and the athletic-only account USD 75. NAIA international registration costs USD 170.
When should I start the eligibility process?
About two years before you finish high school. Create your free profile first and pay for the certification account when a coach shows real interest.
Can a gap year hurt my eligibility?
In Division I it can: the five-year clock keeps running even if you do not play. Plan to enroll the August after you graduate.

title: How Much Does a U.S. College Athletic Scholarship Cover?
h1: How much does a U.S. college athletic scholarship cover?
desc: Athletic scholarships by division (NCAA D1, D2, D3, NAIA, junior college), what international students can and cannot receive, and how to calculate what your family pays.
lead: A "full ride" is rarely just athletic: it usually combines an athletic scholarship, academic merit aid and money from the university itself. Knowing this in advance avoids frustration.
body:
Athletic scholarships by division

NCAA Division I. Since 2025, programs have roster limits instead of scholarship caps, and each university decides how much to offer. Full scholarships exist, but they are highly competitive.

NCAA Division II and NAIA. Almost always partial scholarships. The coach splits a total amount across the whole roster.

NCAA Division III. No athletic scholarships. Aid comes from academic merit or the university, and it can be generous.

Junior college. Cheaper, some offer scholarships, and many players later transfer to a four-year school.

What does not apply to international students

International students cannot receive U.S. federal aid (Pell grants, federal loans). They can receive athletic scholarships, academic merit scholarships and aid from the university itself.

How to calculate what your family pays

Total yearly cost (tuition + housing + food + insurance + flights) − athletic scholarship − academic scholarship − university aid = what your family pays.

Good grades and a strong score on an exam such as the SAT or the Duolingo English Test raise the academic scholarship, which is often added on top of the athletic one.

What to ask the coach about money

How much does the offer cover, and for how many years? Is it renewed automatically? Can I add academic scholarships? Which costs are not covered? What is the final net cost for an international student? Always ask for the offer in writing.
faq: Do international students get athletic scholarships in the U.S.?
Yes. International athletes can receive athletic scholarships, academic merit scholarships and university aid, but not U.S. federal aid.
Which division gives full scholarships?
Division I can offer full scholarships and decides how many to give under roster limits. Division II and NAIA mostly give partial scholarships, and Division III gives no athletic scholarships.
What is an equivalency scholarship?
In sports with equivalency limits, the coach splits a total number of scholarships into smaller portions across the whole roster, so many athletes receive partial awards.
Should I accept an offer without seeing it in writing?
No. Ask for the amount, the duration, the renewal conditions and the costs not covered in writing before you decide.

title: How to Email a U.S. College Coach (With Example)
h1: How to email a U.S. college coach
desc: The structure of a recruiting email that gets read: subject line, what to include, a real example, follow-up timing and the common mistakes international athletes make.
lead: Coaches receive hundreds of emails. Yours has to be readable in 30 seconds and give them a concrete reason to open your video.
body:
The structure

1. Who you are: position, graduation year, country and club. 2. Why that program: something specific (an open spot, the major, the conference). 3. Your key numbers: height, stats, GPA. 4. The link to your video. 5. A closing with one concrete question. Keep it to 150 to 200 words.

The subject line

Short and informative: Class of 2028 GK | Juan Pérez | Argentina | Highlights.

Example

Subject: Class of 2028 GK | Juan Pérez | Argentina | Highlights

Hello Coach Smith,

My name is Juan Pérez, a goalkeeper from Argentina (Class of 2028) playing for Club Atlético Example. I am very interested in [University] because of your [major] program and your team's style of play.

- Height: 6'2" (1.88 m)
- GPA: 3.6 (8.7/10 in Argentina)
- Highlights: [link]

I would love to know if you are still recruiting goalkeepers for the 2028 class and what the next steps would be.

Thank you for your time,
Juan Pérez
[email] · [WhatsApp]

Follow-up

If there is no reply, write again after 10 to 14 days with something new: a new video, a game, a grade update. After that, write whenever you have news to share.

Common mistakes

Sending the same email to everyone without personalizing it, long emails, no video link, not stating your graduation year, and writing to the coach of a different team at the university. International athletes should also state their GPA in U.S. terms or explain their grading scale.
faq: How long should an email to a college coach be?
Between 150 and 200 words: who you are, why that program, your key numbers, your video link and one concrete question.
When should I follow up?
After 10 to 14 days without a reply, and only with something new to share, such as a new video or a game.
Should I email the head coach or an assistant?
Either can work. Replies often come faster from assistant coaches, who usually handle recruiting. Always write to the coach of your own sport and gender.
Do I have to write in English?
Yes. U.S. coaches expect English, and an email in another language is often skipped.

title: How to Make a Highlight Video for U.S. College Recruiting
h1: How to make a highlight video for U.S. college recruiting
desc: Length, order, what to show by position, where to upload it and what to avoid. Practical guide for international athletes recruited by U.S. colleges.
lead: Almost no coach recruits an international athlete without seeing them play. The email opens the door; the video decides whether they reply.
body:
The basics

Length: 3 to 5 minutes. Coaches watch the first 30 to 60 seconds and decide whether to keep going, so put your best plays first. Opening: a 5 to 10 second title card with your name, position, graduation year, height, club, country and email. Identify yourself: before each play, mark who you are with an arrow, a circle or a one-second pause. Use real games over training sessions, against the best opponent possible. Skip loud music and effects.

What to show by position

Goalkeepers: reflex saves, crosses, footwork, one-on-ones and communication. Defenders: recoveries, anticipation, aerial play and clean distribution. Midfielders: line-breaking passes, vision, winning the ball and arriving in the box. Forwards: different kinds of goals, runs, pressing and assists. Basketball: reading the game, shooting, defense and transition. Volleyball: the full action of your position, including setting or passing.

Also add one complete, unedited game: many coaches ask for it after the highlights.

Where to upload it

YouTube (set to Unlisted if you do not want it public), Hudl or Vimeo, with a clear title: "First Last · Position · Class of 2028 · Country". Check that the link opens without asking for permissions, and update it every season.
faq: How long should a recruiting highlight video be?
Between 3 and 5 minutes, with your best plays in the first 30 to 60 seconds.
Should I include a full game?
Yes, as a separate link. Many coaches ask for a complete game after watching the highlights.
Where should I upload my video?
YouTube (unlisted if you prefer), Hudl or Vimeo, with a title that includes your name, position, graduation year and country.
Do I need to pay someone to edit it?
No. A clear, simple edit with identified plays works better than heavy effects.

title: Recruiting Agency vs Doing It Yourself: An Honest Comparison
h1: Sports recruiting agency vs doing it yourself: an honest comparison
desc: What a U.S. college recruiting agency does, what you can do yourself for free with Smartrecruit, and the questions to ask any agency before paying.
lead: Smartrecruit is a website for getting a U.S. college sports scholarship on your own, for free. An agency charges to do part of that work for you. Here are the differences, when each path makes sense and what to ask before paying.
body:
The short answer

College coaches' emails are public, and so are the openings they post. What an agency usually sells is time, organization and guidance. If you are willing to do the process yourself, you can do it for free; if you prefer to delegate, an agency can be an option, but check carefully what it includes.

Comparison

Doing it yourself with SmartrecruitTypical agency model
CostFree with an account.Varies widely and is often paid upfront. Get the price and what it includes in writing.
Coach contactsOfficial emails, with the page each one came from.Often presented as "our own contacts".
Who writesYou, with an English email built from your data.Depends: sometimes them, sometimes you with their template.
OpeningsSearches posted by coaches, filtered by your position.Depends on the agency.
Personal guidanceNo: it is a tool and guides, with no advisor.Yes, it is the main thing they sell.
ResultNo scholarship is guaranteed.Distrust any promise of results: nobody can guarantee a scholarship.

Note: the Smartrecruit app itself is currently in Spanish. The guides and university pages are available in English, and the emails it generates for coaches are always in English.

When doing it yourself makes sense

If you can spend a few hours a week, are comfortable writing short emails in English with a template, and want to understand each step (eligibility, video, follow-up), the do-it-yourself route is the cheapest and keeps you in control.

When an agency can make sense

If you have no time or desire to manage the process, want someone to guide every decision, or your situation is unusual (a transfer, a complicated eligibility case), an advisor can help. In that case, choose carefully.

What to ask an agency before paying

1. What exactly does the price include and exclude? 2. Can I see real examples of athletes with my profile and where they ended up? 3. Who writes to the coaches, and can I see the emails sent? 4. What happens if I get no offers: is there a refund? 5. Do you charge universities or athletes? 6. What contract do I sign, and for how long?

What you have to do either way

With or without an agency, the athlete must register with the eligibility center, keep their grades up, have a good video and reply quickly to coaches. Start with the guides on eligibility, video and how to email a coach.
faq: Do I need an agency to get a U.S. college scholarship?
No. You can contact coaches directly, and many prefer to hear from the athlete. An agency is an option, not a requirement.
Is Smartrecruit an agency?

No. It is a website for doing the process on your own, for free. It is not an agent or an intermediary, does not guarantee scholarships or admission, and is not affiliated with the NCAA, the NAIA or any university.
How do I know if an agency is trustworthy?
Ask for the contract and price in writing and for verifiable examples of athletes they represented, and be wary of guaranteed-scholarship promises or full upfront payments without clear conditions.
Do coaches reply more when the email comes from an agency?
There is no rule. A short, personalized email written by the athlete, with video and key data, often works well. What matters is that it is clear and shows real interest in that program.

title: Are Recruiting Showcases Worth It for a U.S. Scholarship?
h1: Are recruiting showcases worth it for a U.S. scholarship?
desc: What a showcase is, when it can help, when it is wasted money and what to ask before registering. Free alternatives to get noticed by college coaches.
lead: A showcase can help if a specific coach will be there to watch you, but it is not required and it does not guarantee a scholarship. Coaches usually evaluate by video today, so understand what you are buying before you pay.
body:
What a showcase is

An event where athletes play or train to be seen by college coaches. Some are run by agencies, clubs or companies, and each one charges differently and has a different reach.

When it can help

When an interested coach tells you they will attend, when the event lets you play against a level you do not have nearby, or when you want to meet in person a program you already like.

When to think twice

If nobody confirms that a coach at your level and position will attend, if they promise "many coaches will see you" without naming any, or if the cost is high compared with what you can do for free with a good video and direct emails.

What to ask before registering

1. Which universities and coaches will attend, and can I see it in writing? 2. Is it for my sport, position and level? 3. What is the total cost, including travel and lodging? 4. What happens if no interested coach shows up? 5. How is my information sent to coaches afterward?

Free or cheap alternatives

A good highlight video, a list of programs that fit your profile and personalized emails to coaches using this guide. Many coaches prefer that the athlete writes first.
faq: Do I have to attend a showcase to get a U.S. scholarship?
No. You can reach coaches directly with a video and personalized emails.
Do showcases guarantee a scholarship?
No. No scholarship is guaranteed; it depends on level, grades, openings and each coach's decision.
How do I know real coaches attend?
Ask for the list of confirmed universities and coaches in writing and, if you can, email those coaches directly to confirm they will attend.
Does a showcase replace the video?
No. Even if you attend, coaches usually ask for a video to evaluate you, so building one is still a priority.

title: Soccer Scholarships in the U.S. for International Players: Step by Step
h1: Soccer scholarships in the U.S. for international players: step by step
desc: How to get a soccer scholarship at a U.S. college: divisions and scholarships, eligibility, video, how many coaches to contact and how to write to them.
lead: To get a soccer scholarship in the U.S. you need to pick the right level, sort out your eligibility, build a good video and email many coaches yourself. College soccer recruits heavily in South America and beyond, and with persistence you can get there without an agency.
body:
1. Choose your level

There are men's and women's programs in the NCAA (D1, D2 and D3), the NAIA and junior colleges. Division I is extremely competitive. Many international players find their place in Division II, NAIA and junior college, where it is more common to combine athletic and academic scholarships. Smartrecruit lists more than 1,300 men's soccer programs.

2. Understand how scholarships work

In Division II the limit is 9 equivalencies per team in men's soccer and 9.9 in women's, which the coach splits into portions across the roster. Division III offers no athletic scholarships: aid comes from academic merit or the university. In Division I, since 2025-26 and the House v. NCAA settlement, the scholarship cap was replaced by a roster limit of 28 players and each university decides how much to offer. That is why your GPA matters so much: a strong academic scholarship covers what the athletic one does not. More in how much a scholarship covers.

3. Sort out your eligibility

NCAA D1 and D2 require the Eligibility Center; the NAIA has its own registration. Pay special attention to amateurism if you played in the youth system of a club with a professional first team. Everything is in the eligibility guide.

4. Build your video

Three to five minutes, best plays first, identified on every play, plus a full game separately. Follow the video guide.

5. Email many coaches, well

A normal range is 30 to 50 programs that match your level, with a short, personalized email in English, followed up on. Smartrecruit has official emails for more than 1,100 soccer programs and an email generator, though the app is currently in Spanish. Follow the email guide.

Always confirm current rules on the official NCAA and NAIA websites: they change often.
faq: Are there soccer scholarships for international players?
Yes. Universities recruit international players, subject to each governing body's rules and each university's admissions.
How many scholarships does a soccer team have?

In Division II the maximum is 9 equivalencies in men's and 9.9 in women's; Division III has no athletic scholarships; Division I has had a 28-player roster limit instead of a scholarship cap since 2025-26.
How many coaches should I email?
A typical range is 30 to 50 programs that match your level, with personalized emails and follow-up.
Does playing for a club with a professional team hurt me?
It can matter. Review the amateurism section of the eligibility guide, because it can affect your certification.

title: Volleyball Scholarships in the U.S. for International Players: Step by Step
h1: Volleyball scholarships in the U.S. for international players: step by step
desc: How to get a women's volleyball scholarship at a U.S. college: NCAA, NAIA and NJCAA divisions, what coaches look for, the video and how to email them.
lead: To get a volleyball scholarship in the U.S. you need to meet academic eligibility, build a video with full rallies, choose programs at your level and email the coaches yourself. Here is the path, in order.
body:
1. Understand the divisions

Women's volleyball is played in the NCAA (Divisions I, II and III), the NAIA and the NJCAA (junior colleges). Division I and II give athletic scholarships, Division III does not (you can get academic and financial aid), and the NAIA and junior colleges also offer scholarships. In Division II the limit is 8 scholarship equivalencies per team, split into portions by the coach. In Division I, since 2025-26 and the House v. NCAA settlement, the cap went from 12 scholarships to a roster limit of 18 players, and each university decides how much to offer. These rules change, so confirm them on each governing body's official website. More in how much a scholarship covers.

2. Solve eligibility

For NCAA D1 and D2 you must register with the Eligibility Center, and for the NAIA with its own center. Start early. See the eligibility guide.

3. Know the positions and what coaches look at

The main positions are setter, outside hitter, middle blocker, opposite and libero. Coaches look at height, reach and jump, technique, how you read the game and the level you play at. Each program has different openings depending on its players' graduation years, so look at which position each one needs.

4. Build a good video

Show real matches and full rallies with your position clearly identified: serving, passing, defense, attack and, if you are a setter, your setting. Put your best work first, keep it short and add a link to a full match. Follow the video guide.

5. Build your university list

Mix ambitious, realistic and safety programs across divisions. Consider team level, the major you want, cost and openings in your position.

6. Email the coaches

Send a short email in English with your position, graduation year, height, GPA and video link, personalized with something specific to that program. Follow up after 10 to 14 days if there is no reply. The fastest answers often come from assistant coaches. Follow the email guide.
faq: Are there volleyball scholarships for international players?
Yes. Universities can recruit international athletes, subject to each governing body's rules and each university's admissions.
Which division has no athletic volleyball scholarships?
Division III has none; aid comes from academics or financial need. Division II, the NAIA and the NJCAA offer athletic scholarships, and so does Division I under the new rules since 2025-26.
How tall do I need to be to play college volleyball?
There is no single height: it depends on position and division. Setters and liberos are usually shorter than middle blockers. If unsure, email the coach and ask.
When should I start contacting coaches?
As early as possible for eligibility and video. Coaches in each division have rules about when they can contact you first, but you can show interest whenever you want.

title: Softball Scholarships in the U.S. for International Players: Step by Step
h1: Softball scholarships in the U.S. for international players: step by step
desc: How to get a softball scholarship at a U.S. college: divisions and scholarships, positions, what coaches look for, the video and how to email them.
lead: To get a softball scholarship in the U.S. you need to meet eligibility, build a video by position, pick programs at your level and email the coaches yourself. There are thousands of programs, so it pays to start with an organized list.
body:
1. Understand the divisions and scholarships

Women's softball is played in the NCAA (Divisions I, II and III), the NAIA and the NJCAA (junior colleges), among other leagues. Division III gives no athletic scholarships: aid is academic or need-based. In Division II the limit is 7.2 scholarship equivalencies per team, which the coach splits into portions. In Division I, since 2025-26 and the House v. NCAA settlement, the scholarship cap was replaced by a roster limit (25 players in softball) and each university decides how much to offer. Rules change, so confirm them on the official sites. More in how much a scholarship covers.

2. Solve eligibility

NCAA D1 and D2 require the Eligibility Center, and the NAIA has its own. Do it early: see the eligibility guide.

3. Know the positions

Pitcher, catcher, first base, second base, third base, shortstop, outfielders (left, center, right) and designated player. Many players cover more than one position and coaches value that. Each program has different openings depending on its players' graduation years.

4. Build a video by position

Pitchers: show your pitches from two angles, with your pitch types and location. Fielders: fielding, throwing and speed. Hitters: your swing from two angles and real at-bats. Add measurable numbers (pitch speed, time to first base) if you have them. Follow the video guide.

5. Build your university list

Smartrecruit lists more than 1,600 softball programs across all divisions. Build a list of ambitious, realistic and safety programs, and look at the major, the cost and the positions each one needs.

6. Email the coaches

Send a short email in English with your position, graduation year, measurables, GPA and video link, personalized with something concrete about that program. Follow up after 10 to 14 days if there is no reply. Follow the email guide.
faq: Are there softball scholarships for international players?
Yes. Universities can recruit international athletes, subject to each governing body's rules and each university's admissions.
How many scholarships does a softball team have?

It depends on the division. In Division II the maximum is 7.2 equivalencies per team; Division III has no athletic scholarships; Division I has had a 25-player roster limit instead of a scholarship cap since 2025-26. The NAIA and NJCAA have their own rules.
Are softball and baseball the same for recruiting?
No. Women's softball and men's baseball are different sports with their own programs and rules. This guide is about softball.
Which position has the most opportunities?
It depends on each program and year. Pitchers and players who can cover several positions tend to draw more interest, but the best approach is to see what each program needs.

title: Field Hockey Scholarships in the U.S. for International Players
h1: Field hockey scholarships in the U.S. for international players
desc: How to get a field hockey scholarship in the U.S.: it is played only in the NCAA, how many scholarships there are, the video, positions and how to email the coach.
lead: College field hockey in the U.S. is played in the NCAA, with more than 280 programs, and not in the NAIA or the NJCAA. That makes it a sport with few spots, so start early with a well-built list.
body:
1. Where it is played

College field hockey is an NCAA sport (Divisions I, II and III). The NAIA and the NJCAA do not sponsor it; at many of those schools it exists only as a club. There are about 280 NCAA programs, concentrated in the Northeast, the Mid-Atlantic, the Southeast and the Midwest, and very few in California.

2. How many scholarships there are

In Division II the limit is 6.3 scholarship equivalencies per team. Division III gives no athletic scholarships: aid is academic or need-based. In Division I, since 2025-26 and the House v. NCAA settlement, the scholarship cap was replaced by a roster limit of 27 players and each university decides how much to offer. With few spots, many players combine athletic aid with academic aid. Always confirm the rules with each university.

3. Solve eligibility

NCAA D1 and D2 require registration with the Eligibility Center. See the eligibility guide.

4. Positions and what coaches look for

Coaches look for goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders and forwards with good stick skills, game reading and fitness. If you come from a country with a field hockey tradition, your competitive level is an advantage: show it through your club, national team or the tournaments you have played.

5. Build your video

A short video with your best plays, your position clearly identified and your number and jersey visible. Add a full game as a separate link. Follow the video guide.

6. Email the coaches

Smartrecruit lists 284 NCAA field hockey programs. Division I coaches may only contact you starting June 15 after your sophomore year of high school, but you can show your interest earlier. Send a short email in English with your details and video, and follow up after 10 to 14 days. Follow the email guide.
faq: Is there field hockey in the NAIA or the NJCAA?
No. Those leagues do not sponsor it; college field hockey is played in the NCAA.
How many scholarships does a field hockey team have?
In Division II the maximum is 6.3 equivalencies per team; Division III has no athletic scholarships; Division I has had a 27-player roster limit instead of a scholarship cap since 2025-26.
Can international players take part?
Yes. Universities recruit international players, subject to NCAA rules and each school's admissions.
When can a Division I coach contact me?
Under NCAA rules, starting June 15 after your sophomore year of high school. You can show interest earlier, but confirm the current dates with the NCAA.

title: Rugby Scholarships in the U.S. for International Players: How It Works
h1: Rugby scholarships in the U.S. for international players: how it works
desc: College rugby in the U.S.: women's rugby as an NCAA emerging sport, men's rugby mostly club, what scholarships exist and how to contact coaches.
lead: Women's rugby is an NCAA emerging sport, with about 30 varsity programs in 2026, and men's college rugby is mostly club. That changes how players are recruited and what scholarships exist, so understand it before writing to anyone.
body:
1. Women's rugby: an NCAA emerging sport

Women's rugby is an NCAA "Emerging Sport": it does not yet have an NCAA championship, but about 30 programs field it as a varsity team, in Divisions I, II and III. Most compete in the NIRA league and the rest in NCR. The number and mix change every season as programs are added or dropped.

2. Men's rugby: mostly club

In men's college rugby most teams are club teams, run by students with varying support from the university. Some universities have programs with more structure and may offer financial aid, but that is not the norm. Always ask the coach what kind of program it is and what support it gives.

3. What scholarships exist

In NCAA women's rugby, few Division I and II programs can offer athletic scholarships, and fewer give a full one. In most programs aid comes through academic merit or the university's own financial aid, so a good GPA weighs as much as your level of play. In men's rugby, aid is usually academic or from the university rather than a classic athletic scholarship.

4. Solve eligibility

If the program is NCAA (D1 or D2), you must register with the Eligibility Center. Club teams do not require it, but you still need admission to the university. See the eligibility guide.

5. How to show yourself

A match video with your position clearly identified (forwards or backs) and your physical data. If you play for a national team, provincial or regional selections or high-level clubs, put it first. Follow the video guide.

6. Email the coach

Smartrecruit lists 94 men's rugby programs and the NCAA women's rugby programs, with coach contacts available with an account. Send a short email in English with your details and video, and follow up after 10 to 14 days. Follow the email guide.

Always confirm current rules on the official NCAA and NAIA websites: they change often.
faq: Is rugby an NCAA sport?
Women's rugby is an NCAA emerging sport, with about 30 programs in 2026. Men's college rugby is mostly club.
Are there rugby scholarships for international players?
Few programs offer athletic scholarships, and very few give full ones. Many athletes combine a partial scholarship with academic or financial aid from the university.
Do I need the Eligibility Center to play college rugby?
For NCAA programs in Division I or II, yes. For club teams, no, but you still need to be admitted to the university.
What is NIRA?
It is the league that organizes women's rugby for NCAA programs. Other programs compete in the NCR league.

title: Men's Volleyball Scholarships in the U.S. for International Players
h1: Men's volleyball scholarships in the U.S. for international players
desc: How to get a men's volleyball scholarship in the U.S.: few programs, scholarship limits by division, the video, positions and how to contact coaches.
lead: College men's volleyball has far fewer programs than women's, but scholarships can be split into portions and coaches do recruit international players. With few spots, the key is a well-built list and direct emails.
body:
1. Few programs, a lot of competition per spot

College men's volleyball is played in the NCAA (Divisions I, II and III) and other leagues, but there are far fewer programs than in women's volleyball. Many are in California, the Northeast and the Midwest. With fewer spots, write to several programs and also look at schools in lower divisions.

2. How scholarships work

Men's volleyball is an "equivalency" sport: the total scholarship value is split among several players in portions. In Division II the limit is 4.5 equivalencies per team. Division III gives no athletic scholarships: aid is academic or need-based. In Division I, since December 2025 and the House v. NCAA settlement, the scholarship cap was replaced by a roster limit of 18 players and each university decides how much to offer. It is common to combine a partial athletic scholarship with academic aid.

3. Eligibility

NCAA D1 and D2 require registration with the Eligibility Center. See the eligibility guide.

4. Positions and what coaches look for

Setter, outside hitter, middle blocker, opposite and libero. Coaches look at height, jump, technique, game reading and competitive level. If you play in top leagues or national teams in your country, put it on your profile.

5. The video

Real matches and full rallies with your position identified: serving, passing, defense, attack and, if you are a setter, your setting. Follow the video guide.

6. Email the coaches

Send a short email in English with your details and video link, and follow up after 10 to 14 days. Follow the email guide. NCAA contact rules limit when a coach may write to you first, but you can show your interest whenever you like.

Always confirm current rules on the official NCAA and NAIA websites: they change often.
faq: Are there men's volleyball scholarships in the U.S.?
Yes, in Division I and Division II; Division III gives no athletic scholarships. They are split in portions among several players.
How many scholarships does a men's volleyball team have?
In Division II the maximum is 4.5 equivalencies per team. In Division I, since December 2025, there is an 18-player roster limit instead of a scholarship cap.
Are there fewer men's volleyball programs than women's?
Yes, far fewer. That is why it makes sense to look at several divisions and write to several programs.
Can international players take part?
Yes. Universities recruit international players, subject to NCAA rules and each school's admissions.

title: Basketball Scholarships in the U.S. for International Players: Step by Step
h1: Basketball scholarships in the U.S. for international players: step by step
desc: How to get a basketball scholarship at a U.S. college: divisions and scholarships, eligibility, the video and how to contact coaches.
lead: To get a basketball scholarship in the U.S. you need to choose the right level, sort out eligibility, build a video that shows game reading and email the coaches yourself. College basketball has thousands of programs, and choosing where to aim is half the work.
body:
1. Choose your level

There are programs in the NCAA (D1, D2 and D3), the NAIA and junior colleges. Many international players start at a junior college or in the NAIA, adapt to the game and the language, and then move to a four-year university. Smartrecruit lists more than 1,700 men's basketball programs.

2. Understand how scholarships work

In Division II the limit is 10 equivalencies per team, in both men's and women's basketball, which the coach splits into portions. Division III has no athletic scholarships. In Division I, since 2025-26 and the House v. NCAA settlement, the scholarship cap was replaced by a roster limit of 15 players and each university decides how much to offer. More in how much a scholarship covers.

3. Sort out your eligibility

The NCAA and the NAIA have different eligibility centers. If you played for a club with a professional team or were paid anything, read the amateurism section of the eligibility guide carefully.

4. Video: more than points

Coaches want to see game reading, shooting, defense and transition. Include your height and wingspan on the opening title card. Follow the video guide.

5. Contact the coaches

Smartrecruit has official emails for more than 500 basketball programs. Write short, personalized emails in English and follow up after 10 to 14 days. Follow the email guide.

Always confirm current rules on the official NCAA and NAIA websites: they change often.
faq: Are there basketball scholarships for international players?
Yes. Universities recruit international players, subject to each governing body's rules and each university's admissions.
How many scholarships does a basketball team have?
In Division II the maximum is 10 equivalencies per team; Division III has no athletic scholarships; Division I has had a 15-player roster limit instead of a scholarship cap since 2025-26.
Is it a good idea to start at a junior college?
For many international players, yes: it lets you adapt to the game and the language before moving to a four-year university.
What measurements should I put in the video?
Your height and wingspan on the opening title card, and your position and number identified on each play.

title: NCSA vs Smartrecruit: Comparison for International Athletes
h1: NCSA vs Smartrecruit: a comparison for international athletes
desc: What NCSA (ncsasports.org) offers, what Smartrecruit offers and how they differ for an international athlete pursuing a U.S. college scholarship.
lead: NCSA is a U.S. recruiting service with paid memberships; Smartrecruit is a free website for doing the process on your own, built for athletes from Latin America. Each serves a different profile. Here are the differences, without exaggeration.
body:
The short answer

If you want a service with guidance and are willing to pay for a membership, NCSA is a well-known option. If you prefer to do the process yourself, for free, with a focus on athletes from Latin America, Smartrecruit is built for that. Both are independent of the NCAA and of the universities.

Comparison

SmartrecruitNCSA
LanguageThe app is in Spanish; the emails to coaches are generated in English. Guides are available in English and Spanish.Site and content in English.
CostFree with an account.Offers paid memberships. Check its site for the price and what it includes.
FocusAthletes from Argentina and Latin America: international eligibility, GPA conversion and emails in English.A general recruiting service with guides by sport.
Coach contactsOfficial emails with the source of each one.Ask exactly what contact access each plan includes.
Who writes to coachesYou, with an email built from your data.Check how it works on the plan you choose.
Personal guidanceNo: it is a tool with guides, no advisor.Ask what advisory support each plan includes.

When each makes sense

Smartrecruit if you want to save money, understand each step and stay in control, and if you are comfortable with a Spanish-language app. A paid service like NCSA if you want to delegate part of the work and value the guidance. In any case, no service can guarantee a scholarship.

Before paying for any service

Ask in writing what the price includes, how long the contract lasts, what happens if you receive no offers and how to cancel. More questions in the agency comparison.
faq: Is NCSA free?
Its site offers paid memberships. Prices and conditions change, so confirm them on its official page.
Is Smartrecruit affiliated with NCSA?
No. Smartrecruit is independent and is not affiliated with NCSA, the NCAA, the NAIA or any university.
Do I need to pay to contact a coach?
No. Coaches' emails are public and you can write to them directly on your own.
Can I use Smartrecruit and another service at the same time?
Yes. Smartrecruit is free and has no exclusivity.
